title: America's Elites Deserve an
gist: Homeschooling has moved from a quasi-illegal fringe practice to a mainstream, ideologically and religiously diverse educational option (~3.4 million students, 6.3% of school-age kids in 2025), even as prominent media commentators continue to mischaracterize it as a right-wing, anti-institutional phenomenon.

insights.claim: The National Home Education Research Institute estimates around 3.4 million homeschooled students in the US in 2025, roughly 6.3% of the school-aged population.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: A 6%+ share of school-age kids represents a meaningful addressable market for homeschool curriculum, co-op, and ed-tech vendors, plus a growing constituency for school-choice funding policy.
insights.quote: the National Home Education Research Institute estimates that in 2025, there were around 3.4 million homeschooled students in the United States, making up approximately 6.3% of the school-aged population

insights.claim: State-level Education Savings Accounts (ESAs), which let homeschool parents use state funding for approved educational expenses, are expected to further accelerate homeschooling growth.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: ESA expansion is a direct public-funding tailwind for homeschool curriculum providers, tutoring services, and microschools; track state ESA adoption as a leading indicator of homeschool-market growth.
insights.quote: The adoption of “Education Savings Accounts” in many states—which often allow homeschool parents to use state funding to pay for approved educational expenses—promises to further fuel the growth in American homeschooling.

insights.claim: A survey by EdChoice found that one in four homeschooling parents identifies as a liberal Democrat, undercutting the stereotype that homeschooling is exclusively a conservative/evangelical practice.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: Homeschooling's political and demographic diversification broadens its durability as a market/policy trend beyond a single partisan coalition, reducing political tail risk to school-choice funding.
insights.quote: A survey by EdChoice, for example, found that “Among homeschooling parents, one in four identifies as a liberal Democrat.”

insights.claim: According to the National Center for Education Statistics (cited as the National Institute of Education Sciences), homeschoolers were more likely than institutionally schooled peers to visit a library, bookstore, museum, or zoo, contradicting the image of homeschoolers as socially isolated.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: Data undercuts the 'isolated homeschooler' narrative used by critics, suggesting homeschool families are active consumers of cultural/educational institutions and could be a target segment for museums, libraries, and enrichment programs.
insights.quote: homeschoolers were more likely than those in institutional schools to visit a library, go to a book store, go to a museum or art gallery, or go to an aquarium/zoo

insights.claim: Federal centralization of K-12 education in the 1950s was driven by Cold War competitiveness fears ('the next generation of Americans would not be able to defeat the Communists'), and this shift stripped local parents of the education control they had exercised through school boards and PTAs, sowing the seeds of the later homeschool movement.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: Frames homeschooling not as a novel fringe reaction but as a reversion to a century-old norm of parental control, which supports a long-run, structural (not merely cyclical/pandemic-driven) growth thesis for the sector.
insights.quote: this change was caused by a “pressing fear that without a nationally overseen education, the next generation of Americans would not be able to defeat the Communists as their parents had defeated the Nazis.”

insights.claim: The Homeschool Legal Defense Association, founded in 1983 by two attorney fathers, was pivotal in making homeschooling legal in all 50 states and reestablishing parental control over education.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: Marks the legal/regulatory inflection point after which homeschooling could scale nationally without state harassment risk — relevant context for assessing regulatory risk to the sector today.
insights.quote: two homeschooling fathers—who were also attorneys—founded the Homeschool Legal Defense Association in 1983. HLDA was vital to the effort to make homeschooling clearly legal in all 50 states

insights.claim: COVID-era schooling (2020-2021) was the tipping point that pushed homeschooling fully into the mainstream.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: Confirms the pandemic as the demand shock that structurally reset homeschooling's addressable market rather than a temporary blip that should be expected to fully revert.
insights.quote: By 2020-2021, during the COVID pandemic, homeschooling hit the mainstream.

themes.theme: Homeschooling as an institution-adjacent, not anti-institutional, movement

insights.claim: Modern homeschooling in 2026 is 'supra institutional or institution-adjacent' rather than anti-institutional: families often use local schools for select classes, rec sports leagues, and Scouts, treating institutions as optional tools rather than requirements.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: This hybrid-use pattern suggests homeschool families remain a viable customer base for public/private extracurricular and enrichment institutions even as they opt out of core academic instruction — a partial-substitution rather than full-substitution dynamic for traditional schooling budgets.
insights.quote: in many ways, as Lane points out, homeschooling in 2026 is not anti-institutional. Instead, it is supra institutional or institution-adjacent.

insights.claim: The Classical Learning Test (CLT), an alternative to the SAT created by Jeremy Tate, has gained mainstream acceptance in numerous states, an innovation the author says would not have happened without homeschooler demand.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: A concrete example of homeschool-driven demand creating a new, scaling product category (alternative standardized testing) — a template for other homeschool-adjacent product opportunities (curriculum, assessment, credentialing).
insights.quote: the Classical Learning Test, an alternative to the SAT created by Jeremy Tate, has gained mainstream acceptance in numerous states. It is fair to say that this innovation in academic testing would never have happened without the interest and support of homeschoolers.

insights.claim: The author predicts that within the next few decades, virtually every child, regardless of school type, will encounter both homeschooling families and educational changes originally sparked by the homeschool movement.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: Positions homeschooling as a structural force reshaping mainstream K-12 education itself (testing, curricula, flexible schedules), not just a parallel private-choice track — relevant to public-ed policy and ed-tech vendors serving traditional schools.
insights.quote: No matter where a child goes to school in the next few decades, he or she will probably encounter both homeschooling families and educational changes sparked by the homeschool movement.

insights.claim: Popular podcast hosts (Angie Sullivan, Jennifer Welch of 'I've Had It') and CNN's Don Lemon publicly framed homeschooling as inherently 'weird,' distrustful of parents who want to be with their kids, and linked to MAGA/MAHA/tradwife politics and even a 'fascist project,' despite survey data showing broad ideological and demographic diversity among homeschoolers.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: Illustrates a persistent gap between elite media narrative and underlying demographic reality on homeschooling, which could suppress mainstream cultural/political support for school-choice funding even as actual usage grows — a sentiment-vs-fundamentals divergence to watch in education policy debates.
insights.quote: I think it’s just f***ing weird...that you want your kids around you all day, every day and all night.

insights.claim: Johns Hopkins education researcher Angela R. Watson stated publicly that homeschooling data show it is no longer a fringe practice and that homeschoolers are a highly varied population by motive and outcome.
insights.speaker: Ivana Greco
insights.so_what: An academic, non-advocacy source corroborating the mainstreaming thesis strengthens the credibility of a bullish long-run demand case for the homeschool sector.
insights.quote: The data show that homeschooling is no longer a fringe practice ... The honest answer to who homeschools in America is a lot of different people, for a lot of different reasons, with a lot of different results.
insights.locator: quoting Angela R. Watson in The Hill
